items.title: Chuck Mancuso interviewed by Monk Rowe, Buffalo, New York, October 10, 2013
items.q: You know, it helped that John was pushing, Hammond was pushing him all the time.

ctx.x: And here’s a statement you have regarding Benny Goodman. “That Goodman was white and more palatable to the dominant white pop audience should be of little surprise. Even while making a radical shift popular culture seizes upon that which is most accommodating and secure.”

Yeah. Well I think that was part of the culture at the time you know. That’s all. But you know, he brazenly went ahead and he brought in Teddy Wilson. You know, it helped that John was pushing, Hammond was pushing him all the time. But he was a Jewish guy. So he understood it a little better. I always felt that Sicilians understood that stuff too. Because we were swarthy and dark and curly-haired, my people. You know, we had been run over and run by all these other people, which I didn’t know at the time, but…

northern part. Grandpa Giorlamo. They would make fun of him. Oh, you know, where’s your accordion? Where’s your Neapolitan hat? You people smell funny. You do all that. Oh yeah. It was not so nice. And with Sicilians it was worse. It was worse because the Sicilians had an attitude. You know they were run over by the Swedish — the Swedish folks came down and ran the country. And that’s when they had Godfathers. I mean I don’t approve of any of that stuff, but — and I got stories you see, from my grandfather…
